Without Marijuana Prohibition We May Never Have Heard Of Eldridge Cleaver’s Soul on Ice

May 2, 1998

Excerpts from the New York Times obituary:

Leroy Eldridge Cleaver was born in Wabbaseka, Ark., near Little Rock, in 1935…

Cleaver had barely started Junior High School -- where his mother was working as a janitor -- when he was arrested for bicycle theft and sent to reform school...

Almost immediately after his release, he was sent to another reform school, this time for selling marijuana. A few days after he was released from that school he was arrested again, for marijuana possession, and was sentenced to two and a half years at Soledad state prison.

He began his omnivorous reading and received his high school diploma at Soledad, forming, he wrote in "Soul on Ice," "a concept of what it meant to be black in white America…."

Later …

He embraced various religions. He was treated for addiction to crack cocaine in 1990. Another crack arrest two years later was dropped because of an illegal search, but in 1994 Berkeley police found him staggering about with a severe, never fully explained, head injury and a supply of crack in his pocket… He proclaimed himself a conservative and ran, unsuccessfully, for various offices as a Republican.
